Hi Alice — great to connect. Thanks for the options. A couple of quick notes on timezone to avoid any confusion: our team is distributed (US/EU), and with daylight savings differences right now I'd like to confirm the timezone explicitly so no one shows up an hour early/late.

Would you prefer we schedule in UTC (e.g., 09:30 UTC) or include explicit zone labels (e.g., 10:30 CET / 04:30 PDT)? If you're in CET now, the slots you suggested map to:

- Tue Mar 17 10:30 CET = 09:30 UTC
- Tue Mar 17 15:00 CET = 14:00 UTC
- Wed Mar 18 09:00 CET = 08:00 UTC

We have availability for a 30-min demo on Tue Mar 17 at 14:00 UTC (which is 15:00 CET). Aditya (cc'd) will own the demo and I'll join for the discussion on deployment options.

Before I book the invite, quick question: will anyone be traveling/at a conference that week? Travel can shift local phone/hotel times (we've seen people mix up hotel clock vs. home timezone). If so, let us know your preferred canonical timezone to put on the invite.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Marissa — thanks, and good call on the explicit timezones. Quick update:

We're actually onsite at KubeCon this week and I'm currently in San Diego (so my phone's calendar is showing local hotel time, which is PDT). That's why I suggested CET earlier (my default), but that's confusing here. Apologies for the flip-flop.

Availability while at KubeCon (local PDT times):
- Tue Mar 17 — 06:30 PDT (14:30 CET / 13:30 UTC)
- Tue Mar 17 — 12:00 PDT (20:00 CET / 19:00 UTC) [late for EU folks]
- Wed Mar 18 — 08:00 PDT (16:00 CET / 15:00 UTC)

If Aditya can do Tue Mar 17 at 13:30 UTC (my 06:30 PDT), that would work on my side before our morning meetings. Otherwise Wed Mar 18 15:00 UTC is also good.

I've attached the KubeCon session agenda (KubeCon_Agenda.pdf) — we're speaking on Wed afternoon, so timing is tight. Also copied our infra lead Bob so he can confirm.

On another note: hotel clocks are set to local time so my calendar sometimes shows the wrong zone when I create invites from my laptop; I'd prefer you put the invite time in UTC and include both CET/PDT in the event title.

Thanks,
Alice
